title: A spatial magnitude map loses phase and direction
advisorGate: S3B accepted after control repair; S4A selected 2026-09-27
question: What changes when a magnitude map is replaced by independent phase-referenced spatial samples?
model: p(x)=A exp(-ikx)+B exp(ikx); k=2pi f/c; partner coefficients(B*,A*) give conjugate p; global phase multiplies p without changing magnitude

units.p: normalized complex response; no pressure calibration

controls: Single complex sample rank/nullity and explicit kernel
limits: One-dimensional two-traveling-wave model is assumed, not a measured room
Conjugate-swap reverses larger traveling coefficient; known incident direction and passivity may exclude it
Complex samples require common phase reference; sequential phone recordings do not automatically provide one
Recovered coefficients do not identify material, source mechanism or three-dimensional boundaries
incomingEvidence: S2B/S3B scalar fits required gain/timebase premises. This loop adds an independent spatial/phase observable instead of another scalar fit.
